_doc: Read by scripts/check-sycl-alloc-zone-contract.py (clauses e, j and q; later clauses add entries). Permanent exemptions only, each with a reason. An entry names its subject (file and function, or a node key), the raw `name` where the code is E-RAW or E-LIBC, and an exact `count`; it fails if it matches nothing or covers a different number, and `name` pins the allocator so a swapped-in different call does not ride the exemption. Hand-edited; see README.md.

entries.name: mmap
entries.reason: cache bookkeeping, guard-page debug mode, no tensor/KV/scratch/pinned/USM bytes: cache_guard_allocator backs the cache's own hash maps when the guard env is set and falls back to std::allocator; the cache cannot allocate its own map nodes through itself. kv_region_release is noexcept and runs from the plan guard's destructor (the registry release proc): its two catch-all handlers release the replan token and report through kv_region_abort, a named abort, because a release that cannot finish must not propagate out of a destructor. A rethrow of ggml_sycl_fallback_error there would std::terminate without the named message, and the try bodies (registry take, slot-state take_retentions, the retain callback) never raise a planned refusal. Permanent; design docs/design/sycl-kv-region-segregation.md, the registry release proc and the noexcept destructor.

ggml_backend_sycl_plan_caps_new is a C-ABI constructor for the plan-capability handle. Its try body is a bare allocation and counter bump with no planned-refusal path; the handler is the C-ABI boundary, which cannot let an exception cross into the caller and reports failure as a null return. Permanent.

ggml_backend_sycl_plan_scope_open is a C-ABI constructor for the plan scope. Its try body is a bare allocation of the scope object and the filling of its three fields, with no planned-refusal path; the handler is the C-ABI boundary, which cannot let an exception cross into the caller and reports failure as a null return. Permanent.

ggml_backend_sycl_replan_scope_open is a C-ABI constructor for the re-plan scope. Its try body constructs the scope state, whose constructor takes the re-plan token (a mutex acquisition) and raises no planned refusal; the handler is the C-ABI boundary, which cannot let an exception cross into the caller and reports failure as a null return. Permanent.

ggml_backend_sycl_synchronize_for_replan is the public drain a re-plan runs before it publishes: its two handlers log the failed wait and return false, which the caller turns into a refused re-plan. The try body only waits on queues and takes queue-owner mutexes; it never allocates through the planner and raises no planned refusal, so a rethrow would add a second failure path to a boolean contract. Permanent.

ggml_sycl_graph_compute_exit is the graph_compute exit step: its two handlers log and return false, which ggml_sycl_graph_compute_exit_status maps to GGML_STATUS_FAILED. The try body flushes pending scatter state, advances the per-graph caches, publishes staged owners and releases tenant staging; none of it raises a planned refusal, and the exit runs after the compute has already succeeded or failed, so the status is the only channel left. Permanent.

ggml_sycl_graph_compute_exception_exit is noexcept and runs from the cleanup of an exception already in flight: its three catch-all handlers each guard one best-effort drop (the two per-graph caches and the staged-owner retention), because a second exception out of a cleanup would std::terminate and mask the first. None of the three bodies raises a planned refusal. Permanent.

lifecycle_find_probe_placement_plan is noexcept and its try body is a mutex lock plus a map lookup: the catch-all turns a lock failure into a null result, as its sibling lifecycle_find_placement_plan does. It never builds a plan and raises no planned refusal. Permanent.

lifecycle_abort_probe_placement_plan is noexcept and its try body is a mutex lock plus a map erase on the abort path: the catch-all swallows a lock failure so an abort cannot throw out of a cleanup, as its sibling lifecycle_abort_placement_plan does. It raises no planned refusal. Permanent.

unified_cache_raw_device_held_bytes is a read-only accounting query of the runtime allocation registry (the hold ledger's raw-held figure): its try body takes the registry mutex and sums rows, and nothing in it can raise a planned refusal, so there is no refusal for the handler to swallow. It returns the partial sum when the lock fails because a ledger read has no recovery path and must not abort an allocation decision. Permanent; the per-epoch hold ledger design.

allocation_registry_test_publish_raw is a noexcept PRIVATE_TESTING seam that inserts one synthetic row into the runtime allocation registry for tests: its try body only builds the record and takes the registry mutex, so no planned refusal can reach the handler, and a rethrow in a noexcept function would std::terminate. It reports failure by returning false. Permanent; test-only code absent from the shipped library.

C ABI boundary: ggml_backend_sycl_set_runtime_context is a void GGML_BACKEND_API entry and no exception of any type may cross it. Its try body is the runtime-context transaction, which reports a planned refusal through its return value (the result is discarded: the entry has always been fire-and-forget) and names no ggml_sycl_fallback_error, so a rethrow-first clause would guard nothing; the one failure it can raise is the registry lock's std::system_error from the publish tail's drop of the earlier section. The std::exception and catch-all arms log at ERROR with the entry's name and leave the state as the failed path leaves it. Permanent; llama.cpp-moua L4 step 3.

ggml_sycl_published_section_erase is noexcept and runs from ~ggml_backend_sycl_context: its try body is ggml_sycl_published_section_set with a null section (the execution_state_mutex read of the context id and one registry drop_published_section: a map find and an erase, no allocation of device memory and no planned-refusal path), and a rethrow of ggml_sycl_fallback_error out of a destructor would std::terminate. Permanent; llama.cpp-moua L4 step 3.

ggml_sycl_host_tenants_erase is noexcept and runs from ~ggml_backend_sycl_context: its try body takes the context's slot table out of the registry and drops it, which releases carves through their owners' destructors, and nothing in it raises a planned refusal; a rethrow of ggml_sycl_fallback_error out of a destructor would std::terminate. Permanent; llama.cpp-moua L4 step 3c.

ggml_sycl_load_clear_compute_terms is noexcept and runs from the clear guard's destructor at every exit of the load's end call: its try body is a mutex lock and a map erase, with no planned-refusal path, and a rethrow out of a destructor would std::terminate. Permanent; llama.cpp-moua L4 step 3.

ggml_backend_sycl_tenant_coverage is a read-only C-ABI query: its try body parses a descriptor and compares it with the published section, with no allocation of backend memory and no planned-refusal path, and the handler is the C-ABI boundary, which cannot let an exception cross and answers GROWTH, the fail-closed value. Permanent; llama.cpp-moua L4 step 3.

ggml_backend_sycl_load_late_check is a C-ABI comparison of two byte counts through the ledger: its try body reads the open load transaction from the lifecycle registry (admission_diagnostics), takes the ledger mutex and formats a log line, with no allocation of backend memory and no planned-refusal path, and the handler is the C-ABI boundary, which cannot let an exception cross and answers NOT_RECORDED, the fail-closed value. Permanent; llama.cpp-moua L4 step 3.

ggml_backend_sycl_claim_scope_open is a C-ABI constructor for the claim scope: its try body reads the context's slot table from the registry and stores it in a thread_local, with no allocation of backend memory and no planned-refusal path, and the handler is the C-ABI boundary, which cannot let an exception cross and reports failure as the FAILED status, which is distinct from the NO_RESERVATION answer a caller may read as allocate-as-before. Permanent; llama.cpp-moua L4 step 3c.
